claim: Photosynthetic starch reserves that accumulate in Arabidopsis leaves during the day decrease approximately linearly with time at night to support metabolism and growth.
source_text: Photosynthetic starch reserves that accumulate in Arabidopsis leaves during the day decrease approximately linearly with time at night to support metabolism and growth.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations in the manuscript and references to prior work (Gibon et al., 2004; Graf et al., 2010).

claim: The rate of starch decrease is adjusted to accommodate variation in the time of onset of darkness and starch content, such that reserves last almost precisely until dawn.
source_text: We find that the rate of decrease is adjusted to accommodate variation in the time of onset of darkness and starch content, such that reserves last almost precisely until dawn.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, including experiments with unexpected early/late nights.

claim: Generation of starch degradation dynamics requires an arithmetic division computation between the starch content and expected time to dawn.
source_text: Generation of these dynamics therefore requires an arithmetic division computation between the starch content and expected time to dawn.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observed behavior of starch degradation rates adjusting to both starch content and time to dawn.

claim: Mutants with defects in either the accumulation or the degradation of starch have reduced productivity and exhibit symptoms of starvation.
source_text: In the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana this phenomenon is essential for productivity: mutants with defects in either the accumulation or the degradation of starch have reduced productivity and exhibit symptoms of starvation (Usadel et al., 2008; Yazdanbakhsh et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Usadel et al., 2008; Yazdanbakhsh et al., 2011).

claim: Starch content increases approximately linearly with time during the day in Arabidopsis.
source_text: The leaf starch content of Arabidopsis increases approximately linearly with time during the day: more than half of the carbon assimilated via photosynthesis may be stored as semi-crystalline starch granules inside chloroplasts.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by references to prior work (Gibon et al., 2004; Graf et al., 2010).

claim: 95% of starch is utilized by dawn in Arabidopsis.
source_text: At night, starch content decreases approximately linearly with time such that 95% of starch is utilized by dawn (Gibon et al., 2004; Graf et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This quantitative claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The pattern of starch utilization is achieved even when darkness comes unexpectedly early.
source_text: This pattern of utilization is extremely robust, and is achieved even when darkness comes unexpectedly early (Graf et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by both citation to previous work and experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Computation of the appropriate starch degradation rate in a normal night requires the circadian clock.
source_text: Consistent with this idea, we have recently shown that computation of the appropriate starch degradation rate in a normal night requires the circadian clock (Graf et al., 2010), which indicates how information about the expected time to dawn is obtained.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Levels of transcripts for starch-degrading enzymes undergo large daily changes, but levels of the enzymes themselves do not.
source_text: Although levels of transcripts for starch-degrading enzymes undergo large daily changes, levels of the enzymes themselves do not (Smith et al., 2004; Lu et al., 2005; Kötting et al., 2005; Yu et al., 2005; and our unpublished data).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations and unpublished data from the authors.

claim: An arithmetic division mechanism would likely control flux through starch degradation at a post-translational level.
source_text: Therefore, it is likely that an arithmetic division mechanism would control flux through starch degradation at a post-translational level.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation that enzyme levels do not change despite transcript changes.

claim: Post-translational control would permit swifter modulation of the catalytic capacity than would be possible via transcription/translation.
source_text: Post-translational control would also permit swifter modulation of the catalytic capacity of these abundant proteins than would be possible via transcription/translation.
evidence_reasoning: This draws from established understanding of the relative speeds of post-translational vs transcriptional/translational control mechanisms.

claim: The starch degradation system constitutes the first concrete realization of arithmetic operations in biology.
source_text: To the best of our knowledge the starch degradation system constitutes the first concrete realization of such arithmetic operations in biology.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on the authors' assessment of the literature and their findings.

claim: Plants grown in 12-hr light/12-hr dark cycles and subjected to unexpected early darkness (8 hr after dawn) appropriately adjust their starch degradation rate.
source_text: Previously, we showed that the rate of starch degradation is appropriately adjusted in response to an unexpectedly early night (imposition of darkness 8 hr after dawn on plants grown in 12-hr light/12-hr dark cycles)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and citation to previous work.

claim: Plants subjected to unexpected late onset of darkness (16 hr after dawn) also adjust their starch degradation rate appropriately.
source_text: Figure 1A shows starch turnover in Arabidopsis grown in 12-hr light/12-hr dark, then subject to unexpected early (8 hr), normal (12 hr) or unexpected late (16 hr) onset of darkness.
evidence_reasoning: This is shown in the experimental data in Figure 1A, demonstrating adjustment to late darkness.

claim: The cca1/lhy mutant can adjust starch degradation rate in response to an unexpectedly early night.
source_text: Although the rate of degradation is different in a circadian clock mutant with an altered period from that in the wild-type, the capacity to adjust starch degradation in response to an unexpectedly early night is not compromised.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B for the cca1/lhy mutant.

claim: Plants exposed to different daytime light levels adjust their starch degradation rates appropriately.
source_text: Figure 1C shows starch turnover in Arabidopsis exposed to different daytime light levels: 90 µmol quanta m−2 s−1 (open squares) or 50 µmol quanta m−2 s−1 (filled squares)
evidence_reasoning: The experimental data in Figure 1C demonstrates adjustment to different light levels affecting starch content.

claim: Brachypodium distachyon exhibits similar starch degradation adjustment as Arabidopsis when subjected to unexpected early darkness.
source_text: It is also likely that the mechanism underlying this control is present in evolutionarily-distant species of plants.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D for Brachypodium.

claim: A soluble molecule S whose concentration is proportional to the amount of starch in a granule is assumed to exist.
source_text: Hence, we assume the existence of a soluble molecule S whose concentration is proportional to the amount of starch in a granule.
evidence_reasoning: This is a theoretical assumption made for the mathematical models, not directly observed.

claim: A molecule T whose concentration encodes information about the expected time to dawn is assumed to exist.
source_text: Therefore, we further assume the existence of a molecule T whose concentration encodes information about the expected time to dawn.
evidence_reasoning: This is a theoretical assumption made for the mathematical models, not directly observed.

claim: In the first model, the T molecule concentration is proportional to the expected time to dawn after a reset time.
source_text: In our first model the T molecule tracks the time to expected dawn after a reset-time t.
evidence_reasoning: This describes a theoretical model construction.

claim: In the second model, the T molecule concentration increases proportionally to 1/(expected time to dawn).
source_text: In the second model the rT molecule concentration increases with time proportionally to 1/(expected time to dawn)
evidence_reasoning: This describes a theoretical model construction.

claim: Both mathematical models fit the experimental data well.
source_text: The output of this second model is very similar to that of the first model (fits to data of Figure 1A–C shown in Figure 2G,I,K)
evidence_reasoning: The fits of both models to experimental data are shown in Figure 2F-K.

claim: The granule surface area does not limit the reaction rate as the granule shrinks.
source_text: Importantly we assume that the granule surface area does not limit the reaction rate as the granule shrinks, consistent with an approximately linear decrease of starch content with time.
evidence_reasoning: This assumption is made to explain the observed linear decrease in starch content.

claim: The degradation rate is continuously computed via arithmetic division during the night.
source_text: The first prediction is that the degradation rate is continuously computed via arithmetic division during the night.
evidence_reasoning: This is a prediction from the mathematical models.

claim: A night-time light period does not re-entrain the circadian clock.
source_text: We confirmed that the night-time light period did not re-entrain the circadian clock, by monitoring expression of the clock gene LHY
evidence_reasoning: This is confirmed by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: After a night-time light period, the starch degradation rate is reset to accommodate the new starch content and remaining time to dawn.
source_text: The starch degradation rate after the night-time light period was significantly higher than the rate before the light period
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by experimental data in Figure 3 showing rate changes after the light period.

claim: The difference between starch degradation rates after and before the night-time light period is statistically significant (μA − μB = 0.43 ± 0.14 mg g−1 FW/hr, p = 1.6 × 10−3).
source_text: We found μA − μB = 0.43 ± 0.14 (mg g−1 FW)/hr which is significantly greater than 0 (one-tailed Welch's t-test, p = 1.6 × 10−3).
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical analysis of experimental data from the night-time light period experiments.

claim: A factor involved in specifying the relative degradation rates of starch and S molecules must be appropriately set for normal starch degradation patterns.
source_text: The second prediction from the models concerns the effects on starch degradation of perturbations in components of the arithmetic division or degradation apparatus. To reproduce the normal pattern—in which starch is almost completely degraded by the expected time of dawn—our models require that a factor involved in specifying the relative degradation rates of the starch and S molecules must be appropriately set.
evidence_reasoning: This is a prediction derived from the mathematical models.

claim: The lsf1 and sex4 mutants fail to degrade their entire starch reserve at night after prolonged darkness.
source_text: As Figure 4A shows, during the days following the prolonged dark period the mutant plants failed to degrade their entire starch reserve at night.
evidence_reasoning: This is shown in experimental data in Figure 4A.

claim: The lsf1, sex4, bam3, bam4, and isa3 mutants can adjust their starch degradation rate in response to an unexpected early night.
source_text: For five of the six mutants, the rates of starch degradation (as determined from linear fits) were lower during an unexpectedly early night (starting 8 hr after dawn) than in a normal night (starting 12 hr after dawn), as is the case in wild-type plants
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by experimental data in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The pwd mutant does not adjust starch degradation rate in response to an unexpectedly early night.
source_text: However for the sixth mutant, pwd, the rate of starch degradation was not adjusted in response to an unexpectedly early night (Figure 4E,F)
evidence_reasoning: This is shown in experimental data in Figure 4E,F with statistical significance (p = 0.01).

claim: PWD may be a node at which information about expected time to dawn and starch content is integrated to set an appropriate rate of starch degradation.
source_text: This finding indicates that PWD—phosphoglucan, water dikinase—may be a node at which information about expected time to dawn and starch content is integrated to set an appropriate rate of starch degradation.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the experimental observation that pwd mutants cannot adjust degradation rates.

claim: PWD contributes to a cycle of phosphorylation and dephosphorylation of glucosyl residues within starch polymers that is essential for normal starch degradation.
source_text: PWD contributes to a cycle of phosphorylation and dephosphorylation of glucosyl residues within starch polymers that is essential for normal starch degradation.
evidence_reasoning: This draws from established knowledge about PWD function in starch metabolism.

claim: Two enzymes—glucan water dikinase (GWD) and PWD—add phosphate groups to starch polymers at the granule surface.
source_text: Two enzymes—glucan water dikinase (GWD) and PWD—add phosphate groups to starch polymers at the granule surface
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about starch metabolism cited from Smith, 2012.

claim: Two enzymes SEX4 and LSF2 remove phosphate groups from starch polymers.
source_text: and two further enzymes SEX4 and LSF2—remove them.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about starch metabolism cited from Smith, 2012.

claim: Loss of GWD almost completely prevents starch degradation at night.
source_text: All four enzymes are necessary for normal rates of starch degradation, and loss of GWD almost completely prevents degradation at night (Smith, 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Smith, 2012.

claim: Phosphate groups disrupt the ordered packing of starch molecules at the granule surface, allowing access to starch degrading enzymes.
source_text: The phosphate groups are thought to disrupt the ordered packing of the starch molecules at the granule surface, allowing access to starch degrading enzymes (beta-amylases and isoamylase 3).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations (Baunsgaard et al., 2005; Kötting et al., 2005; Ritte et al., 2006; Hejazi et al., 2009) and represents established understanding.

claim: There is a large increase/decrease in the level of phosphate per unit mass of starch over the light/dark cycle.
source_text: Surprisingly, however, we found a large increase/decrease in the level of phosphate per unit mass of starch over the light/dark cycle
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The phosphorylation state of the starch granule surface could provide information about starch content through the day.
source_text: We also showed that the phosphorylation state of the starch granule surface could provide information about starch content through the day.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the experimental observation of changing phosphate levels per unit starch mass.

claim: The analysis may be relevant to a broader class of biological processes where food reserves are just sufficient to permit survival to the expected end of a predictable period.
source_text: Our analysis may also be relevant to a broader class of biological processes, where food reserves accumulated in advance of periods of predictable length without further food intake are just sufficient to permit survival to the expected end of the period.
evidence_reasoning: This is speculative extrapolation of the findings to other biological systems.

claim: Migrating little stints arriving at Arctic breeding grounds have sufficient remaining lipid reserves for an average of only 0.6 days.
source_text: For example, migrating little stints (Calidris minuta) arriving at their Arctic summer breeding grounds after a 5000-km journey have sufficient remaining lipid reserves for an average of only 0.6 days (Tulp et al., 2009).
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from Tulp et al., 2009 as an example of similar biological phenomena.

claim: Male emperor penguins use lipid reserves during a 4-month fast period such that they reach a critical depletion level at approximately the point at which females are expected to return.
source_text: During the 4-month fast period of egg-incubating male emperor penguins (Aptenodytes forsteri), lipid reserves are used such that they reach a critical depletion level at approximately the point at which the females are expected to return.
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from Groscolas and Robin, 2001 as an example of similar biological phenomena.

claim: Analog chemical kinetic approaches may be useful for calculations in synthetic biology applications.
source_text: Analog chemical kinetic approaches may potentially also be useful for calculations in synthetic biology applications (Benenson, 2012), where they are likely to prove much simpler to implement than alternative schemes based on much more complex digital circuitry.
evidence_reasoning: This is speculative discussion about potential applications of the findings.

claim: Previous theoretical implementations of arithmetic operations lacked specific biological applications.
source_text: This contrasts to previous work where elegant theoretical implementations of arithmetic operations lacked specific biological applications (Cory and Perkins, 2008; Buisman et al., 2009).
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparison to previous work cited in the literature.

claim: The number of starch granules per unit volume inside the chloroplast is approximately constant.
source_text: we used the observation that the number of starch granules per unit volume inside the chloroplast is approximately constant, that is, the number of granules n is proportional to the chloroplast volume V (Crumpton-Taylor et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from Crumpton-Taylor et al., 2012 and used as an assumption in the models.

claim: For wild-type plants, the expected value of the ratio R between degradation rates in normal and early nights is approximately 1.33.
source_text: For wild-type plants, the expected value of R is 16/12 ≈ 1.33, that is, the ratio between the expected lengths of the early and the normal night.
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated based on the expected lengths of the night periods.

claim: The pwd mutant has a ratio R of 1.10 ± 0.10, which is significantly different from the wild-type value (p = 0.01).
source_text: Indeed, for this mutant we found that the ratio between the degradation rates (normalized by the respective end-of-light period starch content) during the normal and the early night was R = 1.10 ± 0.10, which is significantly less than the wild-type value (R = 16/12, one-tailed Z-test, p = 0.01).
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical analysis of experimental data for the pwd mutant.

claim: The cca1/lhy mutant has a free-running period of significantly less than 24 hr under continuous light.
source_text: The cca1/lhy mutant has a free-running period of significantly <24 hr under continuous light.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about the cca1/lhy mutant phenotype.

claim: The cca1/lhy mutant exhausts starch reserves around 21-22 hr after the previous dawn instead of 24 hr.
source_text: Indeed, the starch reserve is exhausted around 21–22 hr after the previous dawn, instead of 24 hr as in the wild type.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: LHY transcript levels were slightly elevated during the night-time light period, then peaked about 2 hr later than in plants not exposed to the light period.
source_text: For the experiment shown in Figure 3B, LHY transcript levels were slightly elevated during the night-time light period, then peaked about 2 hr later than in plants that were not exposed to the light period (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence_reasoning: This is experimental data from qPCR analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Arithmetic division can be implemented using analog post-translational chemical kinetics.
source_text: Taken together, our modeling results show that arithmetic division (as well as other arithmetic operations) can be implemented simply using analog post-translational chemical kinetics.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion drawn from the mathematical modeling work presented.
